title: How many wet diapers in days 1–7?
summary: Day-by-day wet diaper counts help you know feeding is on track.
whatsNormal:
In the first week, wet diapers usually increase as milk comes in.

• Day 1: 1 wet diaper
• Day 2: 2 wet diapers
• Day 3: 3 wet diapers
• Day 4: 4 wet diapers
• Day 5–7: 6 or more wet diapers per day

Urine should be pale yellow once milk is in. A few pink-orange spots (urate crystals) can happen in the first days and often clear as feeding increases.
watchFor: Fewer wet diapers than expected for your baby's age in days 3–7
Dark yellow or orange urine after day 4
Lethargy, a very sleepy baby who is hard to wake for feeds
No swallowing sounds during feeds after milk should be in
callDoctorIf: No wet diapers for 12+ hours after day 3
Signs of dehydration: sunken soft spot, dry mouth, no tears when crying
Fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher if under 3 months
You are worried and instincts say something is off, call; that is always OK
